81776.subject: Strengthening Critical Industries
81776.body:
In Context

Автор: J.P. Morgan


Автор: J.P. Morgan

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/strengthening-critical-industries-jpmorgan-boige?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BVXTQhJhWTn%2BlQMnHVpOAHw%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=0MNmsW_c4U8cw1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mvwkgi3a~nd-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mvwkgi3a-nd
  
Geopolitical tensions are reshaping trade patterns and driving higher defense spending. At the same time, the AI race is moving quickly, putting added pressure on critical mineral supply chains and energy grids. Together, these forces have made economic security a top priority for governments and businesses around the world. Against this backdrop, JPMorganChase launched its $1.5 trillion, 10-year Security and Resiliency Initiative (SRI) in October 2025 to support and invest in sectors that are essential to economic security and resilience. One year in, what has the SRI delivered — and what key lessons have emerged? Want more content from In Context? Sign up here 📩 to receive weekly insights directly in your inbox. Leadership lookback: One year of SRI “This is a profound moment for us to do what we do best as a bank: bring together the broad-based capabilities of JPMorganChase and see if we can really make a difference and do it at scale.” — Doug Petno, co-president of JPMorganChase and CEO of the Commercial & Investment Bank Watch the conversation 📽️ By the numbers $230 billion facilitated and financed for projects positioned for rapid construction and scale. $5 billion deployed by the Strategic Investment Group (SIG) to companies strengthening long-term economic security. Roughly 380 transactions completed across critical industries. Four important lessons from year one The past year has underscored that while capital is essential, capital alone is not enough. Ultimately, success requires translating projects from financing to buildout — and scaling them effectively. See the learnings 🔗 Closing the defense production gap A battlefield lesson with boardroom implications — militaries need speed and scale, and the industrial base must keep up. General Chris Cavoli (Ret.), former Supreme Allied Commander Europe, and Mark Marengo, head of Diversified Industries Investment Banking at J.P. Morgan, discuss why closing that gap will require closer partnership between capital, industry and government. Watch the conversation 🔗 Want more content from In Context? Sign up here to receive weekly insights directly in your inbox.
